```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is a first paying customer within 90 days, not a large business. B's consumer subscription at $8–20/month is a low-friction, self-serve purchase. A requires a per-practice B2B sale with a HIPAA BAA executed per customer, which is a much slower path to one paying customer.",
    "The strongest piece of evidence in either brief argues against A. Cydoc was a near-identical product with a clinically credentialed founder. It reached only four paying customers, $27,900 total 2024 revenue (mostly non-subscription), $4,000–$6,000 integration cost per practice, and an estimated 11-year break-even per practice before shutting down. Its first sales call also showed customers renegotiating scope per practice.",
    "B names a cheap, fast, solo-operable channel: Apple Search Ads at about $3.76 average CPA. A's sourced channel is conference exhibiting at $3,000–$10,000 per booth. That is a large upfront cost and a slow loop for a solo operator.",
    "A's regulatory overhead is ongoing per customer (BAAs, safeguards, FDA non-device review). B's regulatory notes are mostly one-time copy and privacy reviews, and they can be reduced further by not targeting clinical populations.",
    "B's weaknesses are real but bear more on long-term viability than on getting one paying customer: an undefined beachhead payer, saturation with free incumbents, and doubtful CAC payback at $8/month. Competitors charging $8–20/month (Yoodli pricing is sourced) show that some consumers do pay in this category."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence rests on one Reddit post. In it, a PMHNP employee says their employer never acted on a request for more pre-intake paperwork. This shows frustration from a non-buyer, not willingness to pay from a practice owner. It is backed only by an AMA statistic quoted secondhand through a competitor's marketing page. The Case For's claim that competitors have 'apparent traction' is not sourced at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A has the better-defined payer and higher sourced price points. If the question rewarded revenue potential over speed to a first customer, A could win. B's demand evidence is also thin: two Reddit quotes and a review hosted on a competitor's own marketing page. Its ASO figure of '$20–50 per acquired user' for an organic channel is internally odd. The deciding factor is the Cydoc precedent, which directly documents how slow and costly A's sales path is."
}
```
